subject: math
title: Repeating Patterns: Find the Core, What Comes Next and Colour-and-Shape Patterns
seo_title: Grade 1 Repeating Patterns Worksheets: AB, AAB, ABC Cores (Free, BC Curriculum Math)
standard_text: Repeating patterns with multiple elements and attributes
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 math worksheets on repeating patterns: find the core of AB, AAB and ABC patterns, say what comes next, work with colour-and-shape patterns, find what is missing and show the same pattern with letters. 100 picture questions with an answer key, matched to the BC curriculum.
key_big: Find the core: the part that repeats. Then say it again and again.
key_sub: Say the core from the start, one thing at a time. When the colour and the shape both change, check both.
body_html:
What is the core?

A repeating pattern has a part that comes again and again. That part is the core. Find the core first. Then say it again and again.

PatternCoreLetters
red, blue, red, bluered, blueA B
clap, clap, stomp, clap, clap, stompclap, clap, stompA A B
drum, bell, shaker, drum, bell, shakerdrum, bell, shakerA B C

What comes next?

Find where the last core stops. Then keep saying the core.

Two things can change

Look at the colour. Look at the shape. Both must match the core.

Example

Red circle, yellow square, blue triangle, red circle, ?

The core has 3 things. After the red circle comes the yellow square. A yellow circle has the right colour but the wrong shape.

Answer: yellow square

What is missing?

Example

Apple, apple, fish, apple, ?, fish

The core is apple, apple, fish. Say it from the start: apple, apple, fish, apple, apple, fish.

Answer: apple

The same pattern with letters

Give each new thing a letter. The first thing is A. The next new thing is B. Then C. Red, red, blue is A A B. Clap, clap, stomp is A A B too. They are the same pattern.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
The wrong core: red, red, blue taken as “red, blue”Find where the whole core starts again
Copying one thing: writing the last thing againSay the core from the start, one thing at a time
Looking at only the colour (or only the shape)Check the colour and the shape every time
Counting on: 1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3, then 4In a repeating pattern, 1, 2, 3 comes back again

faq.q: What patterns do Grade 1 students learn in BC math?
faq.a: In Patterning, BC Grade 1 students work with repeating patterns that have more than one element and attribute, like colour and shape. They find the core, extend the pattern, find what is missing and show the same pattern another way.

faq.q: What is the core of a pattern?
faq.a: The core is the part that repeats. In red, red, blue, red, red, blue, the core is red, red, blue.

faq.q: What does AB, AAB or ABC mean in a pattern?
faq.a: Each letter stands for one thing. Circle, square, circle, square is an AB pattern. Clap, clap, stomp is AAB. Red, yellow, blue is ABC.

faq.q: How can I practise patterns with my child at home?
faq.a: Make patterns with blocks, beads, leaves, rocks or claps and stomps. Ask your child to say the core, what comes next and how to write it with letters.
